title: Interactive books
p: A textbook should let the reader change the thing it explains. MarkdownX has two kinds of live block: a compact Canvas widget driven by JSON, and a full HTML/JavaScript sandbox for everything else.
h1: A Canvas is a small, portable widget
p: This block is stored in DocxXML as an <interactive type="canvas"> element. Its body is JSON, so the same widget runs in the desktop app and in the browser reader without loading a framework.
Move a, b and c. The vertex and the discriminant update with the curve; nothing is pre-rendered. The current runtime also supports unitcircle and projectile.
h1: HTML when the widget needs more freedom
p: The second kind embeds a complete HTML document in a sandboxed iframe. It can draw, animate and respond to pointer events, but it cannot read the book, the library or local files.
Click the sketch to give the pendulum a push. The boundary is deliberate: an HTML block is for a self-contained experiment, not for reaching into the page around it.

“Download as → MarkdownX book (.mdxb)” writes one UTF-8 JSON file. It contains the page tree, both writing formats, images as base64 and these interactive blocks. A reader opens it without an install step:

ol.li: Open web/index.html through a local server, or host the web/ folder.
Drop the .mdxb file on the page, or use “Open a book”.
Switch language and theme in the top bar; the chapter and scroll position are remembered.

callout.p: A book is data, not a build. The desktop editor, the browser reader and future mobile shells all read the same .mdxb; the format is documented in docs/FORMAT.md.

p: 交互书不该只是“能滚动的 PDF”。Canvas 块用 JSON 描述参数，适合公式、图表和物理实验；HTML 块运行在沙箱 iframe 里，适合需要完整 DOM 和动画的实验。导出 .mdxb 时，页面树、两种正文格式、图片和交互块会一起打包，桌面与浏览器阅读器共用同一份文件。
